 Judgment
Dated this the 7th day of August 2025 The appellant is the petitioner in O.P(MV)No.533 of 2017 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Kasaragod.
She claimed compensation under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 for the injuries suffered in a motor accident on 13.07.2017.
On the said day, at about 5.15 p.m., while the Appellant was travelling in an autorikshaw it collided with a car at Periya.
The car came from the opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner and hit against the autorikshaw and thereby, the Appellant sustained injuries.
Respondent Nos.1 & 2 remained ex-parte.
Ext.A1 is the FIR and Ext.A2 is the final report.

As per Ext.A2 report,
the 1st respondent was driving the vehicle bearing registration No.KL-13AG5479 in a rash and negligent manner 2025:KER:60947 and caused the accident.
Therefore, the Tribunal found that the accident happened due to the negligent driving of the 1st respondent.
Thereafter, the Tribunal calculated the compensation for the injuries sustained and awarded a sum of Rs.1,42,250/- with interest @9% from the date of petition till realisation.
Aggrieved by the compensation awarded by the Tribunal, this appeal is filed.
2. The learned counsel for the Appellant submits that that the Appellant was a tailor by profession and was earning an income of Rs.9,000/- p.m.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident, she was unable to work for six months and claimed compensation towards loss of income for that period.
In the absence of any evidence, the Tribunal took Rs.6,000/- p.m. as the monthly income.

The learned counsel relied on the decision of the Apex Court in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram 2025:KER:60947 Alliance Insurance Company Limited [(2011) 13 SCC 236], and submits that the notional monthly income of a coolie who met with an accident in the year 2017 is taken as Rs.11,000/-.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram 2025:KER:60947 Alliance Insurance Company Limited [(2011) 13 SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the Appellant, being a tailor, is entitled to a monthly income higher than that of a coolie.

3. The learned counsel for the respondents opposes the prayer and submits that though the claim was only Rs.9,000/-, the appellant is not entitled to claim more than what was sought in the petition and the benefit of the judgment of the Apex Court is not to enure the benefit of the appellant.
Therefore, the Tribunal has rightly taken the income as Rs.6,000/- p.m.
The Apex Court, in a catena of decisions, has held that even if the claim is less, the compensation to be awarded must be just and reasonable and not based on technicalities.

The Apex Court has fixed the notional income of a coolie in the year 2017 as Rs.11,000/- and therefore, 2025:KER:60947 in the absence of any evidence, the same yardstick can be applied to the appellant.
Therefore, I fix the monthly income as Rs.11,000/-.
Though the appellant claims that there was loss of income for six months, the Tribunal has awarded loss of earnings for three months.

Exts.A7 & A8 wound certificates show that the appellant sustained a fracture of the maxilla, fracture of the zygomatic arch, cerebral concussion and a lacerated wound on the right parietal area of the scalp and that she was hospitalized for five days.
A person, especially a lady, who has suffered injuries to both the head and face, would have to remain at home at least for four months.

Therefore, the loss of earnings is taken for four months @Rs.11,000/- which will Beefathima.H.M vs Mohammed.K.A on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105204252/
2 come to Rs.11,000 x 4 = Rs.44,000/-.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is also argued that though she was treated as an inpatient for five days, she continued her treatment at home for quite a long time and therefore, an amount of Rs.25,000/- was 2025:KER:60947 claimed towards extra nourishment, but the Tribunal did not award anything under this head.
A person who has suffered injuries in an accident and has undergone treatment as both inpatient and outpatient, definitely requires extra nourishment to regain health.
Therefore, taking note of this fact, an amount of Rs.5,000/- is awarded under the head of extra nourishment.
For pain and suffering, though the claim was Rs.50,000/-, the Tribunal has awarded Rs.10,000/-.
Taking note of the injuries which was occurred to the face as well as the head, I award a sum of Rs.10,000/- more under the said head.
4. The learned counsel for the respondents submits that even without a claim for compensation towards amenities and conveniences of life, an amount of Rs.50,000/- was awarded.

It is to be noted that the respondents did not contest the case before the Tribunal and this contention is raised for the first time in this 2025:KER:60947 appeal filed by the claimant, without filing at least a cross- objection.
Therefore, the respondent cannot contend that the award of Rs.50,000/- towards loss of amenities cannot be sustained.
5. The learned counsel for the appellant further argues that she has produced Annexures-A1 and A2 medical prescriptions as well as reports to show that she is still continuing treatment.
However, the fact remains that the said documents do not establish that she had to continue the treatment due to the accident.
Therefore, I am not inclined to grant any amount under future treatments.

Accordingly, the following enhancements/deductions are made to the award passed by the Tribunal:
2025:KER:60947
Sl . Head
of Claim Amt. Awarded Amt. Enhanced No. by Tribunal in appeal (Rs.) (Rs.) 1 Loss of earnings 18,000 44,000 2 Extra Nourishment Nil 5,000 3 Pain and suffering 10,000
A perusal of the award would show that for other heads, just and reasonable compensation has been granted.

In the result, the appeal is allowed and the appellant is entitled for a compensation of Rs.41,000/-
(Rupees Forty One Thousand only) with interest @9% per annum from the date of petition till realisation.
All other findings entered by the Tribunal 2025:KER:60947 stand confirmed.
If any amounts have already been paid, the same shall be granted set off.

The claimants shall produce the details of the Bank account before the Insurance Company/Tribunal within one month from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment and amount shall be transferred to the Bank account directly through NEFT/RTGS mode, within a period of one month thereafter.
If the Bank account is not furnished within the time stipulated, it is made clear that no interest shall run on the enhanced amount after the period stipulated by this Court.
